summary: Restore the missing final digit in 24/215
rationale: 24/21 discusses whom to bring to whom. The supplied 24/215 contains the quoted “Šahrzaman qḥir: Aydarbo kali qume bi qale u zlamano?” with the same combat context. The final digit 5 was omitted.

summary: Correct the English idiom for becoming discouraged
rationale: “Lose one’s heart” means fall in love, whereas “lose heart” means become discouraged. The quoted Turoyo describes lowering his head and becoming upset; the supplied edition says “lässt den Kopf hängen und wird verstimmt”. Removing “his” restores that meaning.

summary: File the imperative “become angry” as detransitive
before: gd-omann-ux ánnaqqa i=qəṣṣa, w k-ubʕət edi áydarbo d-k-ubʕət məqḥár
after: gd-omann-ux ánnaqqa i=qəṣṣa, w k-ubʕət edi áydarbo d-k-ubʕət məqḥár
rationale: The transitive sense is “ärgern” (anger someone), but the imperative məqḥár is addressed to the listener and means “werde so böse, wie du willst”. It illustrates the existing detransitive sense “böse, zornig ... werden”. Retain the imperative form and place it in the corresponding detransitive imperative box.
